From 46cad6cd9b10ab14acf20e0779998f88c6e44c4f Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>
Date: Wed, 22 May 2024 11:49:55 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] irqchip: riscv-imsic: Fixup riscv_ipi_set_virq_range()
 conflict

There was a semantic conflict between 21a8f8a0eb35 ("irqchip: Add RISC-V
incoming MSI controller early driver") and dc892fb44322 ("riscv: Use
IPIs for remote cache/TLB flushes by default") due to an API change.
This manifests as a build failure post-merge.

Reported-by: Tomasz Jeznach <tjeznach@rivosinc.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/mhng-10b71228-cf3e-42ca-9abf-5464b15093f1@palmer-ri-x1c9/
Fixes: 0bfbc914d943 ("Merge tag 'riscv-for-linus-6.10-mw1' of git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/riscv/linux")
Reviewed-by: Anup Patel <anup@brainfault.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240522184953.28531-3-palmer@rivosinc.com
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>

diff --git a/drivers/irqchip/irq-riscv-imsic-early.c b/drivers/irqchip/irq-riscv-imsic-early.c
index 886418ec06cb..4fbb37074d29 100644
--- a/drivers/irqchip/irq-riscv-imsic-early.c
+++ b/drivers/irqchip/irq-riscv-imsic-early.c
@@ -49,7 +49,7 @@ static int __init imsic_ipi_domain_init(void)
 		return virq < 0 ? virq : -ENOMEM;
 
 	/* Set vIRQ range */
-	riscv_ipi_set_virq_range(virq, IMSIC_NR_IPI, true);
+	riscv_ipi_set_virq_range(virq, IMSIC_NR_IPI);
 
 	/* Announce that IMSIC is providing IPIs */
 	pr_info("%pfwP: providing IPIs using interrupt %d\n", imsic->fwnode, IMSIC_IPI_ID);
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

1. **File: `drivers/irqchip/irq-riscv-imsic-early.c`**
   - The line that sets the virtual IRQ range has been modified. The original line:
     ```c
     riscv_ipi_set_virq_range(virq, IMSIC_NR_IPI, true);
     ```
     has been changed to:
     ```c
     riscv_ipi_set_virq_range(virq, IMSIC_NR_IPI);
     ```
   - The boolean parameter `true` has been removed from the function call.

### Relationships Between Modifications

- The modification in `irq-riscv-imsic-early.c` addresses a semantic conflict that arose from changes made in two previous commits. The removal of the boolean parameter in the `riscv_ipi_set_virq_range()` function call resolves the build failure that occurred due to an API change related to the handling of IPIs (Inter-Processor Interrupts) in the RISC-V architecture. This change ensures compatibility with the updated API, thus fixing the conflict and allowing the code to compile successfully.

Here is the commit message:
irqchip: riscv-imsic: Fixup riscv_ipi_set_virq_range()
 conflict

There was a semantic conflict between 21a8f8a0eb35 ("irqchip: Add RISC-V
incoming MSI controller early driver") and dc892fb44322 ("riscv: Use
IPIs for remote cache/TLB flushes by default") due to an API change.
This manifests as a build failure post-merge.

Reported-by: Tomasz Jeznach <tjeznach@rivosinc.com>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/all/mhng-10b71228-cf3e-42ca-9abf-5464b15093f1@palmer-ri-x1c9/
Fixes: 0bfbc914d943 ("Merge tag 'riscv-for-linus-6.10-mw1' of git://git.kernel.org/pub/scm/linux/kernel/git/riscv/linux")
Reviewed-by: Anup Patel <anup@brainfault.org>
Link: https://lore.kernel.org/r/20240522184953.28531-3-palmer@rivosinc.com
Signed-off-by: Palmer Dabbelt <palmer@rivosinc.com>

Here is the root cause:
The bug was caused by a semantic conflict between two commits that modified the API for setting virtual IRQ ranges. Specifically, the function `riscv_ipi_set_virq_range()` was changed to no longer require a boolean parameter, leading to a mismatch in function calls that resulted in a build failure after merging the changes.

Here is the patch:
 
 static int __init imsic_ipi_domain_init(void)
 {
 	int virq;
 
 	/* Create IMSIC IPI multiplexing */
 	virq = ipi_mux_create(IMSIC_NR_IPI, imsic_ipi_send);
 	if (virq <= 0)
 		return virq < 0 ? virq : -ENOMEM;
 
 	/* Set vIRQ range */
-	riscv_ipi_set_virq_range(virq, IMSIC_NR_IPI, true);
+	riscv_ipi_set_virq_range(virq, IMSIC_NR_IPI);
 
 	/* Announce that IMSIC is providing IPIs */
 	pr_info("%pfwP: providing IPIs using interrupt %d\n", imsic->fwnode, IMSIC_IPI_ID);
 
 	return 0;
 }
 #else
